objective: Build WorkPulse - a centralized attendance and leave management system that reduces manual processing for 10,000 employees across office, remote, and field locations. The system must handle 1,000 concurrent clock-ins within 3 seconds, provide payroll-ready monthly exports, enforce attendance policies across multiple time zones, and offer optional facial verification with proper encryption and consent workflows.
architecture:
Users access the Progressive Web Application (Next.js frontend) through HTTPS, which communicates with the Spring Boot API Gateway. Authentication occurs via Microsoft Entra ID SSO or email/password with JWT tokens. The API Gateway routes requests to microservices: Auth Service validates tokens via Redis cache, Employee Service manages profiles in PostgreSQL, Attendance Service processes clock-ins/outs with device data logging and optional facial verification via Azure Face API, Shift Service handles roster assignments, and Leave Service manages approval workflows. 

For offline scenarios: The PWA uses service workers to cache authentication credentials and implements local SQLite database via IndexedDB for queuing operations. Field workers can clock-in/out offline with operations stored locally, then synchronized via Background Sync API when connectivity returns. Conflict resolution uses timestamp-based merging with manager review for discrepancies.

When facial verification is enabled: The Attendance Service calls Azure Face API for verification, stores encrypted biometric templates in PostgreSQL (not raw images), and temporarily processes verification images through S3 encrypted storage which are automatically deleted. Regional compliance workflows enforce jurisdiction-specific consent requirements.

All attendance data flows to PostgreSQL with Redis caching for active sessions. Attendance calculations use UTC timezone-aware engine with timezone_applied tracking. Policy versions with effective dates allow mid-month changes. Daily cron jobs calculate attendance statuses (late, absent, overtime) using current active policies. Monthly batch jobs lock attendance periods and generate payroll exports to S3. Microsoft Entra ID syncs employee data nightly. Notifications go via SendGrid email service. All manual corrections create immutable audit records in PostgreSQL.

techStack.choice: Next.js 15 with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Workbox
techStack.rationale: Next.js provides server-side rendering for fast initial loads and excellent PWA capabilities via next-pwa. Workbox enables robust service worker implementation for offline functionality critical for field workers. TypeScript ensures type safety across complex attendance business logic. Tailwind enables responsive designs for mobile field workers. Alternative: React without SSR would compromise initial load times critical for clock-in speed. Limitation: Next.js hydration overhead increases initial bundle size slightly for mobile users.

techStack.choice: Java Spring Boot 3.3 with Spring Security
techStack.rationale: Spring Boot handles 1,000 concurrent requests efficiently with built-in connection pooling and thread management. Spring Security provides robust RBAC and OAuth2 integration with Microsoft Entra ID. Alternative: Node.js Express would require manual scaling for concurrent clock-ins and lacks built-in enterprise-grade security patterns. Limitation: Spring Boot memory footprint is higher than lightweight alternatives, requiring larger container instances.

PostgreSQL provides ACID compliance for payroll-critical attendance data. TimescaleDB extension optimizes time-series queries for attendance timestamp analysis. Native JSON support stores flexible device metadata and policy versions. Alternative: MySQL lacks native time-series optimizations and JSON query performance. Limitation: TimescaleDB hypertable partitioning adds complexity to standard backup procedures.

Redis provides sub-millisecond response for session validation during clock-in operations. Redis Stack adds RediSearch for complex attendance pattern queries and rate limiting counters. Alternative: Memcached lacks persistence and search capabilities needed for audit trail caching. Limitation: Redis memory usage grows with 10,000 employee sessions, requiring careful eviction policies.

techStack.choice: AWS S3 with SSE-S3 encryption and lifecycle policies
techStack.rationale: S3 provides durable storage for facial verification images with automatic deletion via lifecycle policies. SSE-S3 encryption meets biometric data protection requirements without key management overhead. Alternative: Azure Blob Storage would tie us to Azure ecosystem when other components are AWS-based. Limitation: S3 eventual consistency requires careful handling of immediately deleted temp images.

techStack.choice: Azure Face API (part of Azure Cognitive Services)
techStack.rationale: Azure Face API provides enterprise-grade face verification with Liveness detection to prevent spoofing. Microsoft's compliance certifications cover biometric data processing across multiple jurisdictions. Alternative: AWS Rekognition lacks dedicated liveness detection features critical for attendance fraud prevention. Limitation: Azure Face API costs scale linearly with verification attempts, requiring budget monitoring.

techStack.choice: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) with OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
techStack.rationale: Entra ID integrates with existing enterprise directories and provides SAML/SSO for organizations. OAuth 2.0 flows work with both web and mobile PWA. Alternative: Auth0 would add third-party dependency without native Microsoft ecosystem integration. Limitation: Entra ID custom attribute sync requires nightly batch jobs rather than real-time updates.

SendGrid provides reliable email delivery with templating for attendance notifications. Transactional API handles burst loads during shift change notifications. Alternative: AWS SES requires domain warm-up and lacks built-in templating system. Limitation: SendGrid is a third-party service requiring external dependency monitoring.

techStack.choice: AWS EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) with EC2-backed worker nodes
techStack.rationale: EKS provides Kubernetes orchestration for scaling microservices during peak clock-in periods. EC2-backed nodes eliminate Fargate cold starts, ensuring 3-second response SLA during global morning peaks. Regional pod placement ensures pods are active before timezone workday starts. Alternative: AWS Fargate would cause cold start delays breaching SLA during staggered timezone clock-ins. Limitation: EC2 nodes require more operational management than Fargate.

GitHub Actions integrates with Stark Digital's existing GitHub workflow. AWS CodeDeploy provides blue-green deployments for zero-downtime updates to attendance system. Alternative: Jenkins would require separate infrastructure management. Limitation: GitHub Actions concurrent job limits may slow parallel environment deployments.

userFlow: Employee logs into PWA via Microsoft Entra ID SSO or email/password, receiving JWT token valid for 8 hours cached locally via service worker
Home dashboard displays today's shift timing, next clock-in/out action, and pending leave requests
For clock-in with internet: employee taps 'Clock In', system captures timestamp, device info (browser/OS), IP address, and prompts for optional GPS coordinates
For clock-in offline: PWA stores operation locally in SQLite with timestamp and device info, shows confirmation immediately, queues for background sync
On reconnection: background sync automatically sends queued operations to server, conflict resolution merges based on timestamps with manager review flag for discrepancies
If facial verification enabled: frontend captures image via device camera, sends to Azure Face API for liveness check and verification against enrolled template
On verification success: attendance recorded with 'verified' flag. On failure: fallback to timestamp-only attendance with 'unverified' flag
System prevents duplicate clock-ins within 15 minutes via Redis lock for online, local duplicate detection for offline
Employee views attendance history with color-coded statuses (present, late, half-day, absent) using timezone-aware calculations
Employee requests leave: selects type, dates, enters reason, submits to approval workflow based on department hierarchy
Manager receives email/SMS notification, reviews team attendance dashboard, approves/rejects leave with comments
HR admin configures attendance policies with versioning and effective dates: grace periods, overtime rules, holiday calendars by location
HR creates shift rosters: defines shift patterns with timezone context, assigns employees in bulk, handles overnight shift transitions
Monthly batch process: system calculates final attendance using policy versions active during period, locks period after HR review, generates payroll export CSV
Payroll admin downloads CSV from secured export page or accesses via REST API with API key authentication

dataModel.name: Employee
dataModel.description: Core employee record synchronized from Microsoft Entra ID with manual overrides for HR. Contains reporting structure via manager_id and timezone for base calculations.

dataModel.name: AttendanceRecord
dataModel.description: Daily attendance record with calculated status. device_info stores browser/OS/device model as JSON. status values: present, late, half_day, absent, on_leave. sync_status tracks offline operations: pending, synced, conflict.

dataModel.name: Shift
dataModel.description: Shift definition with timing and policy rules. Times stored in UTC with timezone reference for display. type values: fixed, flexible, night, rotating. is_overnight flag handles date rollover logic.

dataModel.name: ShiftAssignment
dataModel.description: Employee to shift assignment with effective date ranges for roster changes.

dataModel.name: LeaveRequest
dataModel.description: Leave request with multi-level approval workflow. status values: pending, approved, rejected, cancelled. approval_path stores JSON array of approver IDs.

dataModel.name: LeaveType
dataModel.description: Configurable leave types with policy rules. accrual_policy values: monthly, quarterly, annually, none.

dataModel.name: LeaveBalance
dataModel.description: Running balance for each employee's leave types, updated after approvals.

dataModel.name: FacialTemplate
dataModel.description: Encrypted biometric template from Azure Face API. Raw images never stored. jurisdiction_compliance_flags track region-specific requirements (BIPA, GDPR Article 9, etc.).

dataModel.name: AuditTrail
dataModel.description: Immutable audit log for all manual corrections. entity_type values: attendance, leave, shift_assignment. old_value/new_value store JSON diffs.

dataModel.name: Holiday
dataModel.description: Location-specific holiday calendar. is_recurring flag for annual holidays like Christmas.

dataModel.name: Notification
dataModel.description: Notification history for emails/SMS. type values: clock_in_reminder, late_arrival, leave_approval, missing_clock_out.

dataModel.name: AttendancePolicy
dataModel.description: Versioned attendance policies with effective date ranges. Allows mid-month policy changes with retroactive recalculation capability.

dataModel.name: OfflineOperation
dataModel.description: Queue for offline clock-in/out operations. operation_type: clock_in, clock_out. sync_status: pending, synced, conflict. conflict_resolution stores manager override decisions.

pageBehavior.description: Role-specific dashboard: Employees see today's shift, next clock action, recent attendance. Managers see team attendance grid with color-coded statuses, pending leave approvals. HR sees organization-wide metrics: attendance %, late arrivals, leave utilization. All dashboards refresh via WebSocket for real-time clock-in notifications. Offline status indicator shows sync queue count.

Clock-in/out interface with large touch-friendly buttons. Displays current time in employee's timezone. Shows offline capability badge when no internet. If facial verification enabled: shows camera feed with 'Capture' button. On submission: shows spinner for max 3 seconds, then confirmation toast. Includes manual location override button for field workers with poor GPS. Offline submissions show immediate local confirmation.

Calendar view of attendance records with color coding: green present, orange late, red absent, blue on leave. Filter by month, status, timezone view. Export to CSV option. Clicking a day shows detailed record: clock times, device used, verification status, timezone applied. Offline records highlighted with sync status.

Leave request form with date picker showing blocked dates (holidays, existing leave). Real-time balance display updates as dates selected. Required fields: type, dates, reason. Submit triggers approval workflow email notifications.

Manager approval queue showing pending requests from direct reports. Each request shows employee, dates, balance impact, reason. Approve/Reject buttons with comment field. Approval updates attendance calendar immediately. Includes conflict resolution interface for offline attendance discrepancies.

HR shift management: calendar view for assigning shifts to employees. Drag-drop interface for bulk assignments. Overnight shift visual indicator with timezone context. Validation prevents overlapping shifts. Bulk export/import via CSV. Timezone selector for multi-region teams.

HR policy configuration: grace periods, overtime rules, leave accrual rates with versioning. Create new policy versions with effective dates. Location-specific holiday calendar management with recurring pattern setup. Policy history with effective dates and recalculation capability for past periods.

Secured payroll export: month picker shows lock status. Once locked by HR, generates CSV with columns: employee_id, days_present, late_count, overtime_hours, leave_days. Download button and REST API key management for automated systems. Policy version used for calculations displayed.

Audit trail search: filter by date range, entity type, actor. Shows diff view between old/new values. Export full audit logs for compliance. IP address tracking for all manual corrections. Includes offline sync audit logs.

Facial enrollment flow (if enabled): shows jurisdiction-specific consent agreements based on employee location. Camera feed with instructions for neutral expression. Three capture attempts, best template encrypted and stored. Compliance flags set based on regional regulations. Delete enrollment button with confirmation.

Offline sync management: shows queued operations, sync status, conflict resolution interface. Manual sync trigger button. Conflict list showing timestamp discrepancies requiring manager review. Device info for offline operations.

securityDesign: Microsoft Entra ID integration for enterprise SSO with conditional access policies: require MFA for HR/admin roles, location-based restrictions for payroll exports
JWT tokens with 8-hour expiry for PWA sessions, refresh tokens with 30-day expiry stored in HttpOnly cookies, cached locally for offline access via service worker
Role-based access control: Employees see only own data, Managers see direct reports plus one level down, HR sees department scope, System admins see all

Biometric data encryption: Azure Face API templates encrypted at rest using PostgreSQL pgcrypto with jurisdiction-specific compliance flags, keys managed via AWS KMS, raw images auto-deleted from S3 within 1 hour

Regional compliance workflows: Facial enrollment requires jurisdiction-specific consent (BIPA for Illinois, GDPR Article 9 for EU, etc.) with legal review integration. Opt-in per region based on legal assessment

Adaptive rate limiting: Employee_id-based (100/min) combined with IP-based (500/min for corporate IP ranges, 100/min for others). Detects office patterns vs suspicious behavior, auto-adjusts for shift change peaks

Audit trail immutability: AuditTrail records written via database trigger, no update/delete permissions, hashed with previous record hash for chain integrity. Offline operations audit trail maintained
Payroll export security: requires separate 'payroll_export' role, exports logged with recipient email, CSV files encrypted with PGP before S3 storage
OWASP Top 10 mitigation: SQL injection prevention via JPA parameterized queries, XSS protection via React DOM escaping, CSRF tokens for state-changing operations
Network security: VPC isolation for database tier, AWS WAF rules blocking suspicious geographic locations for clock-in attempts. Offline data encrypted locally via IndexedDB encryption

Data retention: Attendance records retained for 7 years via PostgreSQL table partitioning, automated archive to S3 Glacier after 3 years. Biometric templates deleted after consent expiry or employee termination with regional compliance timelines
Offline security: Local SQLite encrypted with Web Crypto API, operations signed with employee session hash, conflict resolution requires manager authentication
deploymentAndOperations: Three environments: Development (auto-deploy on PR merge), Staging (manual promotion for UAT), Production (blue-green deployment via AWS CodeDeploy)
CI/CD pipeline: GitHub Actions runs tests (JUnit, Jest, Cypress), builds Docker images, scans for vulnerabilities (Trivy), deploys to EKS
Monitoring: AWS CloudWatch for infrastructure metrics, Prometheus/Grafana for application metrics (clock-in latency, error rates, offline sync success rate), Sentry for frontend errors

Alerting: PagerDuty integration for 99.9% SLA breaches: clock-in API >3s response time, database connection pool >80% utilization, facial verification failure rate >5%, offline sync backlog >100 operations

High availability design: Minimum 2 pod replicas per service always running on EC2-backed EKS nodes. Regional pod placement ensures pods active before timezone workday starts. Pod pre-warming scheduled 30 minutes before regional morning peaks

Backup strategy: PostgreSQL automated daily snapshots to S3, point-in-time recovery with 35-day retention, tested monthly restore procedure. Local offline database backups via PWA export functionality
Disaster recovery: Multi-AZ EKS cluster, PostgreSQL read replicas in secondary region, failover tested quarterly with clock-in simulation during switch including offline sync recovery

Scaling: Horizontal pod autoscaling based on CPU/memory AND time zone patterns (scale up before regional mornings). Redis cluster autoscaling based on connection count, PostgreSQL read replica scaling for report queries
Maintenance windows: Scheduled via AWS Systems Manager during weekends, employees notified 72 hours prior via email and dashboard banner. Offline mode remains functional during API maintenance
Capacity planning: Monthly review of employee growth vs. resource usage, auto-provisioning triggers at对新60% capacity thresholds. Offline storage capacity monitored per employee device

Compliance operations: Monthly audit log review for unauthorized access attempts, quarterly penetration testing by external security firm, annual regional biometric compliance assessment per jurisdiction
Policy change operations: Policy version deployment includes attendance recalculation batch job for retroactive application. Change management process requires HR approval before activation

timeline.description: Set up AWS infrastructure (EKS with EC2 nodes, RDS, S3), implement Microsoft Entra ID integration, build employee sync service, create PWA skeleton with authentication flows and service worker foundation

Build clock-in/out APIs with device logging, implement shift roster system with timezone-aware logic, create attendance calculation engine with policy versioning, develop basic dashboards, implement offline queuing system with local SQLite

Implement leave types and balances, build multi-level approval workflow, create notification system (SendGrid), develop manager approval interfaces including conflict resolution for offline operations
Integrate Azure Face API, build jurisdiction-specific consent workflows, implement audit trail system, create payroll export functionality with encryption, develop timezone-aware calculation engine

Complete offline sync with background sync API, implement adaptive rate limiting for corporate IP ranges, set up regional pod autoscaling with pre-warming, build policy recalculation engine for mid-month changes

Comprehensive testing: load testing for 1,000 concurrent clock-ins, offline scenario testing, security penetration testing, regional compliance validation, user acceptance testing with real employee scenarios, production deployment and cutover

assumptions: Microsoft Entra ID is available as identity provider with sufficient licenses for all employees
Employees have devices capable of running PWA with camera access for facial verification (optional) and modern browser supporting service workers/IndexedDB
Field workers have intermittent internet connectivity - system implements offline-first design with local storage and background sync
Payroll department accepts CSV export format with predefined columns - no real-time API integration required initially
HR policies can be versioned with effective dates - system supports mid-month changes with recalculation capability
Time zone data is accurate in employee profiles - system tracks timezone_applied per attendance record for travel scenarios
Legal compliance for biometric data is handled via jurisdiction-specific consent workflows with legal team review
Organization has defined reporting structure that fits manager_id hierarchy - no matrix reporting required
Corporate network IP ranges can be identified for adaptive rate limiting configurations
Regional work patterns are predictable enough for pod pre-warming scheduling
openQuestions: What is the exact payroll CSV column format required? Need specification from payroll vendor to ensure compatibility - currently using generic columns
Should facial verification failures trigger automatic manager notifications? Currently silent failure with unverified flag, but fraud prevention might require alerts
How to handle employees working across multiple time zones in same month? Now tracks timezone_applied per record, but need policy for which timezone governs status calculations (profile vs record)
What is the retention period for audit trails? Attendance records 7 years, but audit trails might need longer for compliance investigations
Should there be a mobile device management component to prevent clock-in from unauthorized devices? Currently only logs device info but doesn't restrict
How to integrate with existing HRIS for employee data sync? Currently assumes Entra ID as source of truth, but some fields might need HRIS override
What conflict resolution policy for offline duplicates? Currently timestamp-based with manager review, but need business rules for handling intentional vs system duplicates
How to determine jurisdiction for biometric compliance? Currently based on employee location, but need legal definition of 'work jurisdiction' for remote employees
What corporate IP ranges should receive higher rate limits? Need network team input for office/VPN subnet definitions
How frequently should policy recalculation run for mid-month changes? Currently on-demand but need performance impact assessment
